spec_match.rationale: Contrasts the two real save paths accurately: the download pipeline (where the OnFileDownloaded connector and the Enforce cloud storage verdict live) against File System Access writes, with the download attribute's same-origin rule and the picker's user-activation requirement stated per spec.

interactive.rationale: Both paths run for real from buttons: Path A performs an actual Blob download handoff; Path B genuinely calls showSaveFilePicker and journals each awaited step or the exact rejection.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises the same bytes down both paths with honest fallbacks where the picker is unavailable, which is what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported (typeof undefined), AbortError, SecurityError/NotAllowedError and unexpected-error branches are all handled and labelled; the full success path (picker resolved through close()) cannot be exercised in this automated environment, so its journal wording is verified only by code review here.

references.rationale: Links the ChromeStatus entry, the HTML spec downloading-resources section, and the File System Access spec.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves the anchor/Blob mechanics Path A uses and the absence of any outcome API; picker availability is deliberately not asserted because it is platform-dependent and the page treats absence as an honest reported state, not a failure.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: Path A journalled the 3-row handoff ending in the knowledge-ends row; Path B detected showSaveFilePicker as a function, called it, received SecurityError (no picker in the automated browser) and rendered the labelled amber fallback row plus honest detail text; zero console errors; desktop 1280x2000 and 360x740 DPR3 screenshots read; 0px horizontal overflow at 360.

telemetry_health.rationale: demo-telemetry.js loaded deferred; asserts fire for path-a-handoff and path-b-outcome-labelled (which reports the real outcome token, including the not-observable and refused branches).

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only, buttons override background and color together, comparison table sits in an overflow-x scroller, amber fallback edge uses the shared accent variable.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons, journal is role=log aria-live=polite labelled by the heading, fallback rows are marked in text ('honest fallbacks') not colour alone, table has caption and row/column headers with scope.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x2000: 0px horizontal overflow, buttons wrap, table scrolls internally. Path B's absence on mobile browsers is the demo's own subject matter and is reported as a platform fact on-page, not a broken state.

openQuestions.title: Exercise the picker success path once in headed desktop Chrome
openQuestions.detail: Automated verification reached the SecurityError branch (headless browsers refuse the dialog). Run the page once in headed desktop Chrome via chrome-devtools-mcp or manually, complete a save, and confirm the four success rows (picker resolved / createWritable / write / close) read correctly and the busy-flag prevents double invocation.

guidanceConsulted.query: aria-live status log region for async events
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: One polite live region per page for async outcome announcements; every async state (success, cancel, refusal, unsupported) must surface as perceivable text.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The single role=log journal receives one row per awaited step and one per failure branch, each naming the real DOMException; the output element mirrors the summary politely.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP run transcript shows the SecurityError branch announced as a journal row with the error name quoted.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible file download links and user feedback
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never claim a save succeeded without a real signal; distinguish 'handed off' from 'completed'.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Path A's final row states explicitly that the page cannot know the outcome — the core lesson of the feature — and the comparison table warns against 'saved to your Downloads folder' UI copy.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Journal row: 'Path A: end of the page's knowledge. Disk? Corp Google Drive? Blocked? The page cannot ask and will not be told.'

summary: The migration/edge concept: browser-managed downloads (policy's territory, silent to the page) against page-managed picker writes (step-by-step signals, user-chosen destination). Both paths executed for real under CDP in headless Chromium 141; the picker's refusal there exercised exactly the honest-fallback branch the page is designed around. The success path needs one headed-Chrome pass, recorded as an open question.
